title: Assessing the effects of fluids and antibiotics in an acute murine model of sepsis
author: Jahandideh, Forough
materials:
Overall health will be assessed with the murine sepsis score (MSS)

12
 modified for use in NPSP-01. Briefly, mice will be evaluated for locomotor activity, orbital tightening (indicative of pain or distress from clinical condition), fur appearance (reflective of grooming and hydration), and posture before handling for body weight or temperature measurements. This will be completed at baseline, 4, 6, and 8 hours post-induction. Each mouse will be evaluated at each timepoint by at least two blinded personnel and the calculated mean sepsis score will be used at each timepoint. Body weight and core temperature (as assessed by a rodent rectal probe thermometer) will be measured at baseline, 4 and 8 hours post-induction.

At 4 hours, mice will receive a subcutaneous injection of either buprenorphine alone or a combination of buprenorphine, imipenem-cilastatin, and Ringer’s lactate. Injection volumes will be adjusted according to body weight and experimental group. At the study endpoint (8 hours post-induction) mice will be anesthetized with isoflurane and carotid blood will be collected into EDTA-coated tubes. End point procedures are standardised across centres. Terminal anaesthesia will be induced with isoflurane (5% in an induction chamber followed by 1–2% via nose cone in oxygen at 0.5–1 L/min). The duration of anaesthesia will be recorded in standardised ‘mouse report forms’. Cervical dislocation will be used as a secondary method following anaesthesia to ensure confirmation of death. A portion of the blood will be used for analysis of blood gas and chemistry, while the remaining blood will be used to measure white blood cell counts and bacterial load, and for plasma isolation. Comprehensive biobanking will be performed with up to 20 samples collected per mouse (2-3 samples per tissue). These include plasma, peritoneal lavage fluid, tissues (brain, heart, lung, kidney, spleen, and muscle), and cecal content. Plasma will be prepared by centrifugation of blood at 5000 x g for 10 minutes and will be stored in aliquots of 20 to 100 μL at -80°C. Collected samples will either be stored at -80°C or fixed in formalin at 4°C for a minimum of 24 hours for future histology assessments. Formalin-fixed tissues will subsequently be washed in 1x PBS (Fisher BioReagents, Cat#: BP24384) and stored in either 0.1% sodium azide (VWR Avantor, Cat #: RC7144.8-16) with 30% sucrose (Sigma Aldrich, Cat#: S7903-1KG) (brain samples) or 70% ethanol (Greenfield Global, Cat#: P016EAAN) (all other tissues) for long-term storage.

Training materials: Each center will be responsible for ensuring that its research personnel are adequately trained in experimental techniques including injection protocols, animal handling, monitoring, and tissue collection. To facilitate this training, we have provided training videos and resources. Detailed standard operating procedures were created and shared with all members via a SharePoint (Microsoft, USA) repository to ensure consistent implementation across centers.

Supplies and devices: To reduce confounding due to equipment variability, all necessary supplies (e.g. tubes, vials, EDTA-coated tubes for blood collection, imipenem-cilastatin antibiotic (Sandoz Canada)) as well as devices including thermometers (INTELLIBIO, A-2205-00389), hemocytometers (Hausser Scientific Hemacytometer, #0267151B), Epoc analyzers (Siemens, Model PD470SH-B), and cartridges have been provided by the coordinating center to all participating centers.

steps.title: Acquire and house mice
steps.instruction: Order C57BL/6 mice (10‑12 weeks old) from Charles River (barrier facilities K61/K92). Upon arrival, assess general wellness and exclude any mouse weighing 30 g or failing veterinary health checks. House mice 2‑3 per HEPA‑filtered cage, segregated by sex, with corn‑cob bedding, nesting material, cardboard hut, irradiated Teklad 18 % protein diet, and autoclaved RO water. Maintain cage temperature and humidity as recorded by each facility and change cages every 10‑14 days. Acclimate mice for 4‑6 weeks before experiments.

steps.title: Randomize and ID mice
steps.instruction: Randomly allocate 192 mice in a 1:2:2 ratio (sham + treatment = 36, sepsis = 78, sepsis + treatment = 78) using a computer‑generated stratified permuted‑block design balanced by laboratory and sex. Mark each mouse with a non‑toxic tail marker and record the ID on a mouse report form; verify IDs by a second qualified person.

steps.title: Prepare fecal slurry and vehicle
steps.instruction: Prepare a bulk batch of rat fecal slurry at 100 mg/mL in 5 % dextrose‑10 % glycerol (dextrose‑glycerol) and aliquot into sterile tubes; store at –80 °C. Ship aliquots on dry ice to each center and verify frozen state on receipt before storing at –80 °C. Prepare vehicle aliquots containing 5 % dextrose (Fisher D16‑3) in 10 % glycerol (Fisher BP229‑1), autoclave, and store at –80 °C for sham injections.

steps.title: Prepare syringes (blinded administration)
steps.instruction: One unblinded individual per center prepares the induction (fecal slurry or vehicle) and treatment (imipenem‑cilastatin + Ringer’s lactate) syringes the day before the experiment, labels each syringe with the mouse ID, and discards the allocation list after preparation. A separate blinded individual will later administer the syringes.

steps.title: Induce sepsis or sham (t = 0)
steps.instruction: Anesthetize each mouse with isoflurane (5 % induction, then 1‑2 % maintenance) and inject intraperitoneally into the right or left lower abdominal quadrant using a 26‑gauge needle. For sepsis groups inject fecal slurry at 0.75 mg per gram body weight (≈15 µL of 50 mg/mL slurry per gram; volume up to ~200 µL for 16‑30 g mice). For sham groups inject an equivalent volume of vehicle. After injection, massage the abdomen for 10 seconds, return the mouse to its cage, and place heating blankets set at 37‑38 °C under half of each cage.

steps.title: Baseline and ongoing clinical monitoring
steps.instruction: Record baseline murine sepsis score (MSS), body weight, and core temperature (rectal probe) before injection. Repeat MSS, weight, and temperature assessments at 4 h, 6 h, and 8 h post‑induction. MSS evaluates locomotor activity, orbital tightening, fur appearance, and posture; each time point is scored by at least two blinded observers and the mean is used.

steps.title: Administer analgesia and treatment (t = 4 h)
steps.instruction: At 4 h post‑induction, give all mice a subcutaneous injection of buprenorphine at 0.05 mg/kg (Ceva, DIN 02342510). For mice in the treatment arms also inject imipenem‑cilastatin at 25 mg/kg (Sandoz, DIN 02358344) and Ringer’s lactate at 15 mL/kg (Baxter, DIN 00061085). Adjust injection volumes according to each mouse’s body weight.

steps.title: Humane‑endpoint assessment and early euthanasia
steps.instruction: Continuously monitor for humane‑endpoint criteria: weight loss >20 % from baseline, core temperature drop >20 % from baseline, inability to right when placed on side, labored breathing, average MSS >2.5 for any two criteria, or total average MSS >9.4. If any criterion is met, euthanize immediately with isoflurane anesthesia followed by cervical dislocation and proceed to sample collection.

steps.title: Terminal anesthesia and blood collection (t = 8 h)
steps.instruction: At 8 h post‑induction (or at humane endpoint) anesthetize mice with isoflurane (5 % induction, then 1‑2 % maintenance, 0.5‑1 L/min O₂). Record anesthesia duration. Collect carotid arterial blood into EDTA‑coated tubes, then perform cervical dislocation to confirm death.

steps.title: Process blood and store plasma
steps.instruction: Centrifuge collected blood at 5 000 × g for 10 minutes. Aliquot plasma into 20‑100 µL portions and store at –80 °C until analysis.

steps.title: Collect and biobank tissues
steps.instruction: Perform peritoneal lavage and harvest tissues: brain, heart, lung, kidney, spleen, skeletal muscle, and cecal content (≈2‑3 samples per tissue, up to 20 samples per mouse). Fix tissues in formalin at 4 °C for ≥24 hours. After fixation, wash brain tissue in 1× PBS (Fisher BP24384) and store in 0.1 % sodium azide (VWR RC7144.8‑16) with 30 % sucrose (Sigma S7903‑1KG). Store all other fixed tissues in 70 % ethanol (Greenfield P016EAAN). Unfixed samples are stored at –80 °C.

steps.title: Perform laboratory analyses
steps.instruction: Plate blood and peritoneal lavage on blood agar to quantify bacterial CFU. Count white blood cells manually with a hemocytometer. Measure arterial blood gas and chemistry using the Epoc Blood Analysis System (Siemens PD470SH‑B). Analyze plasma cytokines (IL‑6, GM‑CSF, IFN‑γ, IL‑1β, IL‑2, IL‑4, IL‑10, IL‑12p70, MCP‑1, TNF‑α) and cardiovascular markers (MMP‑9, PAI‑1, PECAM‑1, sP‑Selectin, sE‑Selectin, sICAM‑1, thrombomodulin) by multiplex assay (Eve Technologies).
